title: Genesis close
hook: from a garden to a family in Egypt: God keeps promises through broken people

segments.voice: Yesterday, providence: ye thought evil against me, but God meant it unto good. Your line was meant for good. What did you see grow out of something hard? Day three hundred seventy-six.

Genesis opens with the whole universe: "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." Light, oceans, stars, a garden, two people. Fifty chapters later, it closes on a single box. "So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt." From the heavens to a coffin. From a garden to a foreign country. If you read it as a story about people getting things right, it's a strange ending. But Genesis was never that story. For forty-five days we've walked through it together. Today, the whole book in one look.
screen: `IN THE BEGINNING.` → `A COFFIN IN EGYPT.` → `FORTY-FIVE DAYS.`

segments.voice: It began with light and good and very good, with dust that had breath in it, and a garden to tend and keep. Then a serpent's question, and a God walking in the cool of the day asking, where are you? Coats of skins, made by God, for people who had just disobeyed. Cain and Abel, and the question about being your brother's keeper. Noah building anyway, a dove with an olive leaf, a rainbow that said never again. Babel, where people tried to make a name for themselves. Then the story narrows to one family. Abraham told to go, not knowing where. Stars to count. Hagar, a slave woman, naming the God who sees her. Strangers at Mamre, and Sarah laughing. Abraham arguing with God for a city. Isaac, laughter. A ram on Moriah. Rebekah at the well, Esau and a bowl of stew, Jacob in goat skins, a stairway at Bethel, a wrestling match by a river, a brother who ran. And Joseph: a coat, a pit, a prison, and I am your brother. Look at the people. Liars, schemers, favorites, runaways, brothers who sold a brother. Not one of them is a saint start to finish. And yet the promise God made to Abraham, a family through whom all the families of the earth would be blessed, is still standing on the last page. That is the thread. Broken people, kept promises. And Genesis ends leaning forward. Joseph's last words: God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land. Carry my bones with you when you go. Christians and Jews have both read Genesis as the beginning, not the whole. The coffin waits for a journey.
screen: `A GARDEN, A QUESTION, A FLOOD.` · `ONE FAMILY, ONE PROMISE.` · `LIARS, RUNAWAYS, BROTHERS.` · `CARRY MY BONES WITH YOU.` · then, large: `BROKEN PEOPLE, KEPT PROMISES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: write one line about your own family story. Settle, and breathe. Think of your family, the one you were born into or the one you've made. Its favorites, its feuds, its moves, its surprises. Not the polished version. The real one. Then find one sentence that holds something true about it. Write it down if you can, on your phone or a scrap of paper. If you pray, you can offer that sentence to God. If you don't, just keep it. The bell holds the time.
Genesis close. The end of the book of beginnings: from creation to a family in Egypt, held together by God's promise to Abraham.
Your line: broken people, kept promises. Today, keep one small promise you made, especially one you could quietly let slide. Day three hundred seventy-six.

howItsDone: Christians read Genesis as the opening of the whole biblical story; reading plans that go through the Bible in order begin here and run straight on into Exodus.

original.note: Hebrew: in the beginning. the book's first word, and its name in Hebrew.

trapdoor: what you thought: Genesis is the creation story.
what it means: creation is the first few chapters. most of the book follows one difficult family, and a promise that survives them.
what a scholar hears: the book is built around a repeated heading, these are the generations of, and Joseph's bones are carried out of Egypt in Exodus 13 and buried at Shechem in Joshua 24.
